title: Finiteness of the n-fold relative Frobenius
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, let $S$ be a scheme of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p], and let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For an integer $n\geq1$, let $F_S^n:S\to S$ and $F_X^n:X\to X$ be the n-fold absolute $p$-power Frobenius maps [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Put $X^{(p^n/S)}=X\times_{S,F_S^n,S}S$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $F_{X/S}^{(n)}:X\to X^{(p^n/S)}$ be the unique morphism whose composites with the two projections are $F_X^n$ and $f$, respectively (the n-fold relative Frobenius). Then $F_{X/S}^{(n)}$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0CCD, label lemma-relative-frobenius-finite; Tag 0CCG, label remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius

proof.text: Pull $p=0$ back along $f$ on global sections and restrict to every open to obtain the characteristic of $X$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p]. Write $F=F_S^n$ and $G=F_X^n$ [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. The equality $Gf=fF$ follows on spaces because both Frobenii are the identity, and on sections because ring maps preserve powers. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $r=(G,f):X\to X\times_{S,F}S$ with the two required projection equations and proves its uniqueness.

The absolute iterate $G$ is affine: the inverse image of each affine open is that same affine open, since $G$ is the identity on the space. Its map on sections is $s\mapsto s^{p^n}$. Every section $s$ of the inverse image satisfies the monic polynomial $T^{p^n}-s$ with coefficients mapped by $G^\sharp$, since its evaluation is $s^{p^n}-s^{p^n}=0$. The exponent $p^n$ is nonzero because $p$ is prime. This proves integrality directly from [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], without any finite-type hypothesis on the absolute Frobenius.

source.place: Tag 0CC8, lemma-frobenius: direct monic-equation argument for the n-fold iterate

proof.text: The same identity-on-spaces observation makes $F$ affine. By clauses (1) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], its base change $\pi_1:X\times_{S,F}S\to X$ is affine and separated. Now $r\pi_1=G$ is integral by the preceding step, so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-of-comp-separated] gives integrality of $r$. This replaces successive twists and integral composition by cancellation against a separated projection.

The second projection $\pi_2$ satisfies $r\pi_2=f$. The latter is locally of finite type by hypothesis, so clause (f) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] proves that $r$ is locally of finite type. No hypothesis on $\pi_2$ is required.

Combine the integrality and local finite type of $r$ using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-iff-integral-lft] to obtain finiteness. Together with the projection identities and uniqueness from the first step, this proves exactly the stated n-fold relative Frobenius assertion.

The Lean proof is by F6, 2026-10-19.
